title: Bandwidth ladder
idea: From narrowest to widest: CW, SSB, FM, fast-scan TV. Each step up is a big jump.

config.heading: How wide is each signal?
config.lead: Each step on the scale is ten times wider. Tap a signal for its number.

bands.name: Signal width
bands.text: CW, then SSB, then FM, then fast-scan TV. SSB is narrower than FM. The scale is in kHz.

segs.label: FM voice on repeaters
segs.text: An FM voice signal on VHF repeaters is between 10 and 15 kHz wide, wider than SSB.

marks.label: CW
marks.text: CW needs about 150 Hz. It's the narrowest signal.

marks.label: SSB voice
marks.text: A typical SSB voice signal is about 3 kHz wide. The receiver filter with the best signal-to-noise ratio for SSB is 2400 Hz.

marks.label: AM fast-scan TV
marks.text: AM fast-scan TV is about 6 MHz wide.

bands.title: Narrowest to widest

traps.why: SSB is narrow, but CW is narrower still.

traps.wrong: SSB signals are easier to tune in correctly
traps.why: The difference the exam wants: SSB has a narrower bandwidth than FM.
FM voice on repeaters is 10 to 15 kHz. 150 is a CW number, in Hz.
AM fast-scan TV is about 6 MHz.
2.4 kHz is the SSB filter. CW needs about 150 Hz.
500 Hz would cut off SSB voice. 2400 Hz matches the signal for the best signal-to-noise.
